questions.prompt: How does the scheduling policy decide whether an appointment fits a working-hours rule when local time, dates and midnight are involved?

keyPoints.text: Appointments are stored as two increasing instants, while working hours are local rules: weekday plus start and end minute in a named timezone.
keyPoints.quote: weekday plus start and end minute in a named timezone

keyPoints.text: Turning an instant into a local clock loses information unless the local date is kept, which is what dateKey is for.
keyPoints.quote: loses information unless the local date is retained too

keyPoints.text: An appointment may end exactly at the following local midnight when the rule ends at minute 1440.
keyPoints.quote: may end exactly at the following local midnight

keyPoints.text: To accept that midnight, the code checks the instant immediately before the endpoint is still on the starting day; every other cross-date interval is closed.
keyPoints.quote: Any other cross-date interval is closed.

keyPoints.text: Seconds and milliseconds count in the minute comparisons, so an end just past a boundary cannot slip through by truncation.
The zoned endpoints are computed in the staff timezone with hourCycle h23 before the rule comparison.

questions.prompt: Explain why daylight-saving transitions and the h23 hour cycle matter to this algorithm.

keyPoints.text: The formatter uses hourCycle h23 without hour12, so midnight is 00 rather than 24 in labels and arithmetic.
keyPoints.quote: Midnight is therefore represented as 00 rather than 24

keyPoints.text: A DST boundary changes the relationship between local clock time and UTC.
keyPoints.quote: A DST boundary changes the relationship between local clock time and UTC

keyPoints.text: That is why the tests include a spring-transition local midnight and a folded clock interval.
keyPoints.quote: a spring-transition local midnight and a folded clock interval

keyPoints.text: Intervals whose local end clock is not later than the start are rejected.
keyPoints.quote: Intervals whose local end clock is not later than the start are rejected

keyPoints.text: The rejection of folded intervals happens before any rule is consulted.

questions.prompt: How do overlap, cancellation and validation fit together, and what does the availability grid promise?

keyPoints.text: Overlap is half-open: a meeting ending at 10:00 may sit right before one starting at 10:00, while positive overlap is blocked.
The SQL exclusion constraint uses the same interval convention for BOOKED rows, and cancelled rows do not occupy the calendar.
keyPoints.quote: canceled rows do not occupy the calendar

keyPoints.text: Validation is separate from availability: a well-formed interval can legitimately be unavailable.
A zero step or invalid timestamp is malformed and must fail promptly, never loop forever or return an empty preview.
keyPoints.quote: never produce an infinite loop or an apparently valid empty preview

keyPoints.text: The availability grid is anchored to whatever from the client sends, not to the start of working hours.
keyPoints.quote: The grid is therefore anchored to whatever

keyPoints.text: Every closed slot gets the same blocked reason, whatever the cause.
